93-070.r: 'Das Capital' → Karl Marx (19th-century economist and philosopher); theory of the capitalist system; second and third volumes edited after his death by Friedrich Engels.

93-071.r: Not by Ambedkar: 'Servants of India' (by R.K. Laxman). Ambedkar wrote Thoughts on Pakistan, Annihilation of Caste, The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution.

93-072.r: 'Vanguard' → émigré communist journal of M.N. Roy, who founded the Communist Party of India at Tashkent.

93-073.r: Anandmath (Bankim Chandra) → linked with rise of national movement; contains Vande Mataram. Bankim's first novel → Durgesh Nandini (1865, Bengali).
93-073.t: Satyarth Prakash → Dayananda; Gita Rahasya → Tilak; Gitanjali → Tagore; only Anandmath fits the national-movement tag here.

93-076.r: 'Rajaniti Ratnakara' → Chandesvara. Kirtilata, Kirtipataka and Purusha Pariksha → Vidyapati.

93-077.r: 'Kissa Radha Kanhaiya' (Radha Kanhaiya Ka Kissa) → Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.

93-078.r: Anand Math (Bankim Chandra Chatterjee) → 'Bible of Bengali Patriotism'; based on Sanyasi Rebellion (1763-1800); contains National Song 'Vande Mataram'.

93-080.r: 'Desher Katha' (S.G. Deuskar, in Bengali) → warned against colonial 'hypnotic conquest of the mind'; inspired Swadeshi street plays and folk songs. 'Desh' was not Bengal-specific.

93-081.r: 'Chetavani Ra Chugatiya' → Kesari Singh Barahath, poet and freedom fighter of Rajasthan.

93-082.r: Gandhi's autobiography 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' → originally written in Gujarati.

93-084.r: 'Hind Swaraj' → Gandhi wrote it in Gujarati in 1909, on a ship from London to Cape Town; banned by the British, so translated into English.

93-086.r: 'Bharat Durdasha' → drama by Bharatendu Harishchandra, famous 19th-century Hindi author.

93-087.h: Bharatendu's two plays: Bharat Durdasha and Andher Nagari.

93-088.r: Subramaniam Bharati → great Tamil poet; his songs were used during the Swadeshi Movement.

93-089.r: 'Bharat Bharati' → 'Rashtrakavi' Maithili Sharan Gupta; other works: Panchavati, Saket, Yashodhara, Jayadrath Vadh.

93-091.r: Not a pre-independence nationalist poet: Shiv Kumar Batalvi (Punjabi poet and playwright). Ranglal, Nabin Chandra Sen, Hem Chandra Banerjee were nationalist poets.

93-092.r: Wrong: Nabin Chandra Das's play 'Nawab' was about a bankrupt Nawab, not Bengal famine. True: Neel Darpan → indigo farmers; Ghashiram Kotwal → Vijay Tendulkar; Urdu theatre relied on Parsi theatre.

93-093.r: 'Towards Struggle' and 'Prison Diary' (1975) → Jayaprakash Narayan ('Loknayak'); gave the Total Revolution (Sampurna Kranti) slogan in 1974.

93-095.r: 'A Passage to India' → E.M. Forster; novel set against British rule and the freedom movement in 1920s India.

93-098.r: 'Indian National Movement: The Long-Term Dynamics' → Bipin Chandra, historian of modern India.

93-099.r: 'The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India' (economic policies of national leadership, 1880-1905) → Bipin Chandra.

93-100.r: 'Out of Print: Newspapers, Journalism and the Business of News in the Digital Age' → Professor George Brock.

93-101.r: 'Mother India' → Catherine Mayo. Unhappy India → Lajpat Rai; Geeta Rahasya → Tilak; Memories of My Life and Times → Bipin Chandra Pal.

93-102.r: Indian War of Independence 1857 → V.D. Savarkar; Anand Math → Bankim Chandra Chatterjee; The Life Divine → Sri Aurobindo; Sadhana → Rabindranath Tagore.

93-103.r: 'Jhanda Geet' (Vijayi Vishwa Tiranga Pyaara, Jhanda Uncha Rahe Humara) → Shyamlal Gupta 'Parshad'.

93-105.r: 'Aie Mere Watan Ke Logo' → poet Pradeep (Ramachandra Narayanji Dwivedi, born Ujjain); tribute to soldiers martyred in the 1962 Indo-China war.

93-106.r: 'Saare Jahan Se Achcha' → Muhammad Iqbal, born 9 Nov 1877 at Sialkot, Punjab; poet and lawyer who later joined the Muslim League.

93-108.r: 'Mazhab Nahi Sikhata Aapas Mein Bair Rakhna' → a line of Muhammad Iqbal's 'Saare Jahan Se Achcha'.

93-109.r: Bhojpuri poem 'Firangiya' against British colonialism → Manoranjan Prasad Singh.

93-110.r: Pamphlet 'Why I Am an Atheist?' → Bhagat Singh.

93-111.r: 'Amar Sonar Bangla' → Rabindranath Tagore, during Bengal partition movement (1905); Bangladesh adopted its first 10 lines as National Anthem. Tagore also composed Jana Gana Mana.
93-111.h: Tagore: anthem-writer for two nations, India (Jana Gana Mana) and Bangladesh (Amar Sonar Bangla).

93-113.r: 'The Golden Threshold' (collection of poems) → Sarojini Naidu.

93-114.r: 'Songs from Prison' (English translations of Sanskrit hymns, Upanishads) → Mahatma Gandhi, made in Yeravada Prison, 1932.

93-115.r: 'Landmarks in Indian Constitutional and National Development' → Gurmukh Nihal Singh, also first Governor of Rajasthan (1956-1962).

93-116.r: 'Congress Presidential Addresses' (two parts: 1885-1910 and 1911-1934) → edited by G.A. Natesan.

93-117.r: Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' while imprisoned in Ahmednagar Fort Jail.
93-117.t: Not Naini, Alipur or Yervada jail: Discovery of India = Ahmednagar Fort.

93-118.r: Catherine Mayo → Mother India; Collins and Lapierre → Freedom at Midnight; Ram Manohar Lohia → Guilty Men of India's Partition; Jawaharlal Nehru → The Discovery of India.

93-120.r: 'Bandi Jivan' (based on revolutionary movements) → Sachindranath Sanyal.

93-121.r: 'Mountbatten and the Partition of India' → Larry Collins and Dominique Lapierre.

93-122.r: 'Journey through the Kingdom of Oudh in 1849-50' → W.H. Sleeman, British administrator; published in two parts in London.

93-123.r: 'The Indian War of Independence 1857' → V.D. Savarkar, who called 1857 the first freedom struggle; R.C. Majumdar did not see 1857 as a freedom struggle.

93-124.r: R.C. Dutt: Economic History of India under Early British Rule; J.R. McLane: Indian Nationalism and the Early Congress; B.N. Ganguli: Indian Economic Thought; Bipin Chandra: Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism.

93-125.r: 'Planned Economy for India' → M. Visvesvaraya; suggested a ten-year plan for India in 1934.

93-126.r: 'The Roots of Ancient India' → Walter A. Fairservis Jr.; on prehistoric cultures of the subcontinent.

93-127.r: 'JP Movement - Emergency and India's Second Freedom' (on Loknayak Jayaprakash Narayan) → written by M.G. Devasahayam.
93-127.c: No answer printed: the author, M.G. Devasahayam, is not among the options.

93-128.r: Priya Pravas → Ayodhya Prasad; Gaban → Prem Chand; Eternal India → Indira Gandhi; Shah Nama → Firdausi.

93-129.r: Autobiography of an Unknown Indian → Nirad C. Chaudhari; India: A Wounded Civilization → V.S. Naipaul; Confessions of a Lover → Mulk Raj Anand; The English Teacher → R.K. Narayan.

93-130.r: 'Planning and the Poor' → B.S. (Bagicha Singh) Minhas.

93-131.r: 'Problems of the Far East: Japan-Korea-China' → George N. Curzon.

93-132.r: 'The Untold Story' (published 1967, on the 1962 India-China war) → Lt. General Brijmohan Kaul.

93-133.r: 'The Alphabet: A Key to the History of Mankind' → British linguist David Diringer.

93-134.r: 'A Gallery of Rascals' → Ruskin Bond (born 19 May 1934); Sahitya Akademi Award 1992 for 'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra'.

93-135.r: 'The Proudest Day: India's Long Road to Independence' → Anthony Read and David Fisher.

93-136.r: My Music My Life → Pt. Ravi Shankar (autobiography); Adha Gaon → Rahi Masoom Raza; Radha → Ramakant Rath; The Pilferer → Laxman Gaikwad.
